- **Files Changed**: 13
- **Additions**: +331
- **Deletions**: -149
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T13:49:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T13:49:56Z

## PR Description

Closes #2
## What changed

Initial routing system: the app boots on a Start page that leads into a Shell page hosting the 4 main destinations — home, explore, collection, profile.

## Key decisions

- Built-in named routes (`MaterialApp.routes`, `lib/routing/app_routes.dart`) — no new dependencies for the initial system
- `StartPage` uses `pushReplacementNamed` so back-from-shell doesn't return to the start screen
- `ShellPage` switches destinations with a `NavigationBar` + `IndexedStack`, so each tab's state survives switches
- Destination order driven by the `ShellDestination` enum; pages are placeholders for future stories
- Replaced the template counter page and its smoke test with routing/shell widget tests

## How to verify

```bash
flutter test        # 10 widget tests pass
flutter analyze     # no issues
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[main] --> APP[DarkCatsFactoryApp]
  APP -->|"/"| START[StartPage]
  APP -->|"/shell"| SHELL[ShellPage]
  START -->|pushReplacementNamed /shell| SHELL
  SHELL --> NAV[NavigationBar]
  SHELL --> STACK[IndexedStack]
  STACK --> H[HomePage]
  STACK --> E[ExplorePage]
  STACK --> C[CollectionPage]
  STACK --> P[ProfilePage]
```

</details>

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **Updated**: 2026-10-20T13:49:56Z

## PR Description

Closes #2
## What changed

Initial routing system: the app boots on a Start page that leads into a Shell page hosting the 4 main destinations — home, explore, collection, profile.

## Key decisions

- Built-in named routes (`MaterialApp.routes`, `lib/routing/app_routes.dart`) — no new dependencies for the initial system
- `StartPage` uses `pushReplacementNamed` so back-from-shell doesn't return to the start screen
- `ShellPage` switches destinations with a `NavigationBar` + `IndexedStack`, so each tab's state survives switches
- Destination order driven by the `ShellDestination` enum; pages are placeholders for future stories
- Replaced the template counter page and its smoke test with routing/shell widget tests

## How to verify

```bash
flutter test        # 10 widget tests pass
flutter analyze     # no issues
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[main] --> APP[DarkCatsFactoryApp]

  APP -->|"/shell"| SHELL[ShellPage]
  START -->|pushReplacementNamed /shell| SHELL
  SHELL --> NAV[NavigationBar]
  SHELL --> STACK[IndexedStack]
  STACK --> H[HomePage]
  STACK --> E[ExplorePage]
  STACK --> C[CollectionPage]
  STACK --> P[ProfilePage]
```

</details>

Now let me look at key review points:

1. **`.gitignore` change**: adds `/input/` and `/outputs/` — agent harness artifacts. This is scope creep relative to "create initial routing system"? It's minor housekeeping, probably fine but worth noting. Actually it's reasonable to exclude these. But it's in the diff — it's arguably out of scope for a routing PR. Minor.

2. **`lib/app.dart`**:
  - `initialRoute: initialRoute` — passing nullable string. If null, MaterialApp uses default `/`. Fine.
  - `MaterialApp` without `onGenerateRoute` — unknown routes will crash in debug / show error. For a routing PR, missing `onUnknownRoute` handling. Minor/suggestion.
  - The `initialRoute` param is test-only — documented. OK.
  - Theme duplicated? The old main.dart had theme with deepPurple seed; new app.dart keeps it. Fine.

3. **`lib/main.dart`** — now just boots the app. Fine.

4. **`lib/routing/app_routes.dart`**:
  - `abstract final class AppRoutes` with static consts. Fine, modern Dart.
  - Route `start = '/'`. Note: with `MaterialApp.routes` and `initialRoute` default `'/'`, the `/` route is the start page. OK.
  - Potential issue: `onGenerateRoute` not set; deep links to unknown routes → error page. Minor.

5. **`lib/pages/shell_page.dart`**:
  - `enum ShellDestination { home, explore, collection, profile }` — public enum used to drive order.
  - `_icons` map uses records `(IconData, IconData)`.
  - `_icons[destination]!` — null assertion; safe because map covers all values. Could use `._` lookups... fine.
  - `capitalize` extension is private (unnamed extension `extension on String`). It's defined in the same file at the bottom. Private extension in a page file — could be a util. Minor.
  - `ShellDestination.values[index]` — index from NavigationBar; safe.
  - **Potential issue**: `IndexedStack` keeps all 4 pages mounted — fine for placeholders, but state claim "each tab's state survives" — yes.
  - **Deep-link/URL issue**: with named routes, `/shell` state (selected tab) isn't in the route. Not a big deal for this stage.
  - **Important correctness nuance**: `Navigator.of(context).pushReplacementNamed(AppRoutes.shell)` — then within ShellPage, back button (Android system back) exits app. Fine.
  - `_pages` is `static const Map<ShellDestination, Widget>`; `_pages.values.toList(growable: false)` — the order of Map literal values follows insertion order which matches enum order. OK.
  - The tuple `_icons[destination]!.$1` and `.$2` — using record positional fields; a bit cryptic; could be a small data class or two maps. Suggestion-level.

6. **`lib/pages/start_page.dart`**:
  - `pushReplacementNamed` — good.
  - The button label 'Start' — fine.

7. **Tests**:
  - `test/app_test.dart` — 4 tests.
  - `test/shell_page_test.dart` — 6 tests. Total 10 — matches PR description "10 widget tests".
  - `tapDestination` uses `find.text(label).last` — why `.last`? Because the label text may also appear in page content (e.g., 'Home' text in HomePage center and in NavigationBar). Actually pages show text 'Home', 'Explore', etc. So `find.text('Explore')` matches both the nav label and the page text. `.last` picks the NavigationBar one (nav bar is later in tree? Actually body is built before bottomNavigationBar in Scaffold... but with IndexedStack offstage pages also present). Hmm, `find.text('Explore')` before tapping: initially only 'Explore' nav label visible (ExplorePage offstage? No — IndexedStack mounts all children, so ExplorePage's Text('Explore') is in the tree but offstage). By default `find.text` has `skipOffstage: true`, so initially only the NavigationBar label matches. After navigating to Explore, both are visible... wait, but in tapDestination, we tap before the page is shown, so only nav label visible at tap time. `.last` is defensive. But wait — `find.text('Collection')` when tapping Collection initially: only nav label. OK.
  - In the 'shell offers the four destinations' test they use `find.descendant(of: navigationBar, matching: find.text('Home'))` — good scoping.
  - `testWidgets('home is the initial destination')` — expects ExplorePage findsNothing — works due to skipOffstage default true.
  - Tests look reasonable. One britleness: `tapDestination` with `.last` relies on widget order; fine.
  - No test for Android back from shell returning to... pushReplacement means back exits. No test needed.
  - No `flutter_test` config for fonts/assets; fine.

8. **Missing things**:
  - No `onGenerateRoute`/`onUnknownRoute`: navigating to an undefined route throws. For initial routing system, might be worth a suggestion.
  - `AppBar`? Shell has no app bar — placeholders.
  - The `capitalize` extension is `extension on String` (unnamed/private) — usable only within shell_page.dart. Fine but if needed elsewhere later, move to a shared util. Suggestion.
  - Potential a11y/semantics: NavigationBar destinations fine.
  - `Colors.deepPurple` — matches template. Fine.

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

Closes #2
## What changed

Initial routing system: the app boots on a Start page that leads into a Shell page hosting the 4 main destinations — home, explore, collection, profile.

## Key decisions

- Built-in named routes (`MaterialApp.routes`, `lib/routing/app_routes.dart`) — no new dependencies for the initial system
- `StartPage` uses `pushReplacementNamed` so back-from-shell doesn't return to the start screen
- `ShellPage` switches destinations with a `NavigationBar` + `IndexedStack`, so each tab's state survives switches
- Destination order driven by the `ShellDestination` enum; pages are placeholders for future stories
- Replaced the template counter page and its smoke test with routing/shell widget tests

## How to verify

```bash
flutter test        # 10 widget tests pass
flutter analyze     # no issues
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
  M[main] --> APP[DarkCatsFactoryApp]

  SHELL --> NAV[NavigationBar]
  SHELL --> STACK[IndexedStack]
  STACK --> H[HomePage]
  STACK --> E[ExplorePage]
  STACK --> C[CollectionPage]
  STACK --> P[ProfilePage]
```

</details>

Clean — no leftover references to the removed `MyApp`/`MyHomePage`, no secrets patterns. README doesn't mention the counter.

Now, deep-review analysis. Let me think through the findings carefully:

### Findings candidates:

**1. `_icons[destination]!` null assertions + records `.$1`/`.$2`** (shell_page.dart:55-58)
- Safe at runtime since map covers all enum values, but `!` assertions and positional record accessors `.$1`/`.$2` are unreadable and fragile if a new enum value is added without an icon entry (runtime crash at first build of that destination). Alternative: exhaustive switch expression — Dart exhaustiveness checking on enums would make adding a new destination a compile error. This is a real maintainability point. IMPORTANT or SUGESTION?
 - A `switch (destination)` expression over an enum is exhaustively checked by the compiler; a map lookup with `!` fails only at runtime. For a codebase intended to grow (4 destinations, future stories), the switch is meaningfully safer. But it's still "works as shipped" → per verdict rules: correctness/bug findings = BLOCKING only if broken behavior. This is a latent-crash risk on future extension, not current bug. I'd rate IMPORTANT (real maintainability debt).

**2. `capitalize` private extension in shell_page.dart** (line 72-74)
- Unamed `extension on String` in a page widget file. Works, but it's a general-purpose string utility living in shell_page.dart; when another file needs capitalization they'd copy it. Also unnamed private extension silently applies to all Strings in this file. Move to `lib/common/` or name it. SUGESTION.

**3. `_pages.values.toList(growable: false)`** (line 48)
- Depends on map insertion order implicitly. Since Dart maps preserve insertion order it's correct, but a `List` constant (or `IndexedStack(children: [...])` derived from an iterable of destinations) would make the "order == enum order" contract explicit. Could merge with finding 1 as one comment about enum-driven lookups. Actually I'll keep them separate but small.

Actually, let me consolidate: one inline comment on shell_page.dart build method / maps about exhaustive switch instead of map+`!`. And maybe a separate one about the extension.

**4. MaterialApp lacks `onGenerateRoute`/`onUnknownRoute`** (app.dart:23-28)
- With `routes:` map only, navigating to an undefined route (deep link typo, future code calling pushNamed('/settings')) throws in debug and shows red screen. Since this PR is "initial routing system", wiring `onGenerateRoute` centralizing route resolution (or at least `onUnknownRoute`) would be the natural foundation. SUGESTION/IMPORTANT? The PR scope is initial routing; unknown-route handling is arguably part of a routing foundation. But it's not a bug today — all navigation goes through defined constants. I'd say SUGESTION. Hmm. For an "initial routing system" PR, adding onUnknownRoute early is cheap and prevents future crashes. But severity-wise: no current breakage → SUGESTION.

**5. `initialRoute` param "used by tests"** (app.dart:9-12)
- Test-only production parameter. It's a common, pragmatic pattern; documented. SUGESTION-level at most. Actually it's fine — many projects do this; the doc comment explains it. Skip or mention as fine. I'll skip — not a finding. Hmm, alternatively could suggest `@visibleForTesting` annotation to enforce. That's a nice small suggestion: annotate with `@visibleForTesting`? No wait — it's a constructor param used by tests only, annotating the field with `@visibleForTesting` is exactly the idiomatic way to encode "used by tests". Good small SUGESTION with concrete fix.

**6. `.gitignore` adds `/input/` and `/outputs/`** — unrelated to routing (harness housekeeping). Minor scope note. Given the repo is an agent-factory repo, it's pragmatic; the PR description doesn't mention it. SUGESTION-level note (scope transparency) or skip? The guidelines say flag scope creep. It's 3 lines, harmless, and self-documented ("Agent task harness artifacts (not part of the app)"). I'd note it in general comment, not inline. Or a tiny inline suggestion. I'll include as SUGESTION inline on the .gitignore line, asking to either mention it in PR description or split. Actually per the diff checklist "Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep?" — yes flag it, but SUGESTION severity.

**7. Test britleness: `tapDestination` uses `find.text(label).last`** (shell_page_test.dart:19-22)
- `.last` relies on widget-tree order to disambiguate the NavigationBar label from page content text (pages show the same strings: 'Home', 'Explore'...). Currently at tap time the target page is offstage so `find.text` (skipOffstage:true) matches only the nav label; `.last` is unnecessary-but-defensive. Scoping with `find.descendant(of: find.byType(NavigationBar), matching: find.text(label))` would be explicit and immune to future page content that contains the label text (very likely: a Profile page will contain the word "profile", etc.). Once a page with visible text 'Home' exists, `.last` may pick the wrong one (actually page text comes before NavigationBar in the tree? Scaffold body before bottomNavigationBar → `.last` = NavigationBar label. Still fragile but currently right). SUGESTION.

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 3
- **URL**: https://github.com/Vovanella95/dark_cats_factory/pull/3
- **Title**: gh-2 Create initial routing system
- **Author**: Vovanella95
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-2` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 13
- **Additions**: +331
- **Deletions**: -149
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T13:49:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T13:49:56Z

## PR Description

Closes #2
## What changed

Initial routing system: the app boots on a Start page that leads into a Shell page hosting the 4 main destinations — home, explore, collection, profile.

## Key decisions

- Built-in named routes (`MaterialApp.routes`, `lib/routing/app_routes.dart`) — no new dependencies for the initial system
- `StartPage` uses `pushReplacementNamed` so back-from-shell doesn't return to the start screen
- `ShellPage` switches destinations with a `NavigationBar` + `IndexedStack`, so each tab's state survives switches
- Destination order driven by the `ShellDestination` enum; pages are placeholders for future stories
- Replaced the template counter page and its smoke test with routing/shell widget tests

## How to verify

```bash
flutter test        # 10 widget tests pass
flutter analyze     # no issues
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[main] --> APP[DarkCatsFactoryApp]
  APP -->|"/"| START[StartPage]
  APP -->|"/shell"| SHELL[ShellPage]
  START -->|pushReplacementNamed /shell| SHELL
  SHELL --> NAV[NavigationBar]
  SHELL --> STACK[IndexedStack]
  STACK --> H[HomePage]
  STACK --> E[ExplorePage]
  STACK --> C[CollectionPage]
  STACK --> P[ProfilePage]
```

</details>

## PR Description

Closes #2
## What changed

Initial routing system: the app boots on a Start page that leads into a Shell page hosting the 4 main destinations — home, explore, collection, profile.

## Key decisions

- Built-in named routes (`MaterialApp.routes`, `lib/routing/app_routes.dart`) — no new dependencies for the initial system
- `StartPage` uses `pushReplacementNamed` so back-from-shell doesn't return to the start screen

- Destination order driven by the `ShellDestination` enum; pages are placeholders for future stories

- `StartPage` uses `pushReplacementNamed` so back-from-shell doesn't return to the start screen
- `ShellPage` switches destinations with a `NavigationBar` + `IndexedStack`, so each tab's state survives switches
- Destination order driven by the `ShellDestination` enum; pages are placeholders for future stories
- Replaced the template counter page and its smoke test with routing/shell widget tests

## How to verify

```bash
flutter test        # 10 widget tests pass
flutter analyze     # no issues
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[main] --> APP[DarkCatsFactoryApp]
  APP -->|"/"| START[StartPage]
  APP -->|"/shell"| SHELL[ShellPage]
  START -->|pushReplacementNamed /shell| SHELL
  SHELL --> NAV[NavigationBar]
  SHELL --> STACK[IndexedStack]
  STACK --> H[HomePage]
  STACK --> E[ExplorePage]
  STACK --> C[CollectionPage]
  STACK --> P[ProfilePage]
```

</details>"
  }
}

blocks.text:
Now I have the full diff. Let me review the changed files deeply. Let me also look at the project structure, AGENTS.md (if it exists), and the instructions.md at repo root (mentioned in guidelines).

Let me check:
1. instruction.md at repo root — project stack, conventions
2. AGENTS.md — coding styles
3. The repo structure

Interesting: In the diff of `lib/main.dart` removed code, I see `colorScheme: .fromSeed(seedColor: Colors.deepPurple)` and `mainAxisAlignment: .center` — this is Dart's new dot-shorthand syntax (Dart 3.10 feature). The removed code had it, so the template was created with a newer Flutter. That's fine.

Now let me look at key review points:

1. **`.gitignore` change**: adds `/input/` and `/outputs/` — agent harness artifacts. This is scope creep relative to "create initial routing system"? It's minor housekeeping, probably fine but worth noting. Actually it's reasonable to exclude these. But it's in the diff — it's arguably out of scope for a routing PR. Minor.

2. **`lib/app.dart`**:
  - `initialRoute: initialRoute` — passing nullable string. If null, MaterialApp uses default `/`. Fine.
  - `MaterialApp` without `onGenerateRoute` — unknown routes will crash in debug / show error. For a routing PR, missing `onUnknownRoute` handling. Minor/suggestion.
  - The `initialRoute` param is test-only — documented. OK.
  - Theme duplicated? The old main.dart had theme with deepPurple seed; new app.dart keeps it. Fine.

3. **`lib/main.dart`** — now just boots the app. Fine.

4. **`lib/routing/app_routes.dart`**:
  - `abstract final class AppRoutes` with static consts. Fine, modern Dart.
  - Route `start = '/'`. Note: with `MaterialApp.routes` and `initialRoute` default `'/'`, the `/` route is the start page. OK.
  - Potential issue: `onGenerateRoute` not set; deep links to unknown routes → error page. Minor.

5. **`lib/pages/shell_page.dart`**:
  - `enum ShellDestination { home, explore, collection, profile }` — public enum used to drive order.
  - `_icons` map uses records `(IconData, IconData)`.
  - `_icons[destination]!` — null assertion; safe because map covers all values. Could use `._` lookups... fine.
  - `capitalize` extension is private (unnamed extension `extension on String`). It's defined in the same file at the bottom. Private extension in a page file — could be a util. Minor.
  - `ShellDestination.values[index]` — index from NavigationBar; safe.
  - **Potential issue**: `IndexedStack` keeps all 4 pages mounted — fine for placeholders, but state claim "each tab's state survives" — yes.
  - **Deep-link/URL issue**: with named routes, `/shell` state (selected tab) isn't in the route. Not a big deal for this stage.
  - **Important correctness nuance**: `Navigator.of(context).pushReplacementNamed(AppRoutes.shell)` — then within ShellPage, back button (Android system back) exits app. Fine.
  - `_pages` is `static const Map<ShellDestination, Widget>`; `_pages.values.toList(growable: false)` — the order of Map literal values follows insertion order which matches enum order. OK.
  - The tuple `_icons[destination]!.$1` and `.$2` — using record positional fields; a bit cryptic; could be a small data class or two maps. Suggestion-level.

6. **`lib/pages/start_page.dart`**:
  - `pushReplacementNamed` — good.
  - The button label 'Start' — fine.

7. **Tests**:
  - `test/app_test.dart` — 4 tests.
  - `test/shell_page_test.dart` — 6 tests. Total 10 — matches PR description "10 widget tests".
  - `tapDestination` uses `find.text(label).last` — why `.last`? Because the label text may also appear in page content (e.g., 'Home' text in HomePage center and in NavigationBar). Actually pages show text 'Home', 'Explore', etc. So `find.text('Explore')` matches both the nav label and the page text. `.last` picks the NavigationBar one (nav bar is later in tree? Actually body is built before bottomNavigationBar in Scaffold... but with IndexedStack offstage pages also present). ## PR Description

Closes #2
## What changed

Initial routing system: the app boots on a Start page that leads into a Shell page hosting the 4 main destinations — home, explore, collection, profile.

## Key decisions

- Built-in named routes (`MaterialApp.routes`, `lib/routing/app_routes.dart`) — no new dependencies for the initial system
- `StartPage` uses `pushReplacementNamed` so back-from-shell doesn't return to the start screen
- `ShellPage` switches destinations with a `NavigationBar` + `IndexedStack`, so each tab's state survives switches
- Destination order driven by the `ShellDestination` enum; pages are placeholders for future stories
- Replaced the template counter page and its smoke test with routing/shell widget tests

## How to verify

```bash
flutter test        # 10 widget tests pass
flutter analyze     # no issues
```

```mermaid
  SHELL --> NAV[NavigationBar]
  SHELL --> STACK[IndexedStack]
  STACK --> H[HomePage]
  STACK --> E[ExplorePage]
  STACK --> C[CollectionPage]
  STACK --> P[ProfilePage]
```

</details>

Clean — no leftover references to the removed `MyApp`/`MyHomePage`, no secrets patterns. README doesn't mention the counter.

Now, deep-review analysis. Let me think through the findings carefully:

### Findings candidates:

**1. `_icons[destination]!` null assertions + records `.$1`/`.$2`** (shell_page.dart:55-58)
- Safe at runtime since map covers all enum values, but `!` assertions and positional record accessors `.$1`/`.$2` are unreadable and fragile if a new enum value is added without an icon entry (runtime crash at first build of that destination). Alternative: exhaustive switch expression — Dart exhaustiveness checking on enums would make adding a new destination a compile error. This is a real maintainability point. IMPORTANT or SUGESTION?
 - A `switch (destination)` expression over an enum is exhaustively checked by the compiler; a map lookup with `!` fails only at runtime. For a codebase intended to grow (4 destinations, future stories), the switch is meaningfully safer. But it's still "works as shipped" → per verdict rules: correctness/bug findings = BLOCKING only if broken behavior. This is a latent-crash risk on future extension, not current bug. I'd rate IMPORTANT (real maintainability debt).

**2. `capitalize` private extension in shell_page.dart** (line 72-74)
- Unamed `extension on String` in a page widget file. Works, but it's a general-purpose string utility living in shell_page.dart; when another file needs capitalization they'd copy it. Also unnamed private extension silently applies to all Strings in this file. Move to `lib/common/` or name it. SUGESTION.

**3. `_pages.values.toList(growable: false)`** (line 48)
- Depends on map insertion order implicitly. Since Dart maps preserve insertion order it's correct, but a `List` constant (or `IndexedStack(children: [...])` derived from an iterable of destinations) would make the "order == enum order" contract explicit. Could merge with finding 1 as one comment about enum-driven lookups. Actually I'll keep them separate but small.

Actually, let me consolidate: one inline comment on shell_page.dart build method / maps about exhaustive switch instead of map+`!`. And maybe a separate one about the extension.

**4. MaterialApp lacks `onGenerateRoute`/`onUnknownRoute`** (app.dart:23-28)
- With `routes:` map only, navigating to an undefined route (deep link typo, future code calling pushNamed('/settings')) throws in debug and shows red screen. Since this PR is "initial routing system", wiring `onGenerateRoute` centralizing route resolution (or at least `onUnknownRoute`) would be the natural foundation. SUGESTION/IMPORTANT? The PR scope is initial routing; unknown-route handling is arguably part of a routing foundation. But it's not a bug today — all navigation goes through defined constants. I'd say SUGESTION. Hmm. For an "initial routing system" PR, adding onUnknownRoute early is cheap and prevents future crashes. But severity-wise: no current breakage → SUGESTION.

**5. `initialRoute` param "used by tests"** (app.dart:9-12)
- Test-only production parameter. It's a common, pragmatic pattern; documented. SUGESTION-level at most. Actually it's fine — many projects do this; the doc comment explains it. Skip or mention as fine. I'll skip — not a finding. Hmm, alternatively could suggest `@visibleForTesting` annotation to enforce. That's a nice small suggestion: annotate with `@visibleForTesting`? No wait — it's a constructor param used by tests only, annotating the field with `@visibleForTesting` is exactly the idiomatic way to encode "used by tests". Good small SUGESTION with concrete fix.

**6. `.gitignore` adds `/input/` and `/outputs/`** — unrelated to routing (harness housekeeping). Minor scope note. Given the repo is an agent-factory repo, it's pragmatic; the PR description doesn't mention it. SUGESTION-level note (scope transparency) or skip? The guidelines say flag scope creep. It's 3 lines, harmless, and self-documented ("Agent task harness artifacts (not part of the app)"). I'd note it in general comment, not inline. Or a tiny inline suggestion. I'll include as SUGESTION inline on the .gitignore line, asking to either mention it in PR description or split. Actually per the diff checklist "Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep?" — yes flag it, but SUGESTION severity.

**7. Test britleness: `tapDestination` uses `find.text(label).last`** (shell_page_test.dart:19-22)
- `.last` relies on widget-tree order to disambiguate the NavigationBar label from page content text (pages show the same strings: 'Home', 'Explore'...). Currently at tap time the target page is offstage so `find.text` (skipOffstage:true) matches only the nav label; `.last` is unnecessary-but-defensive. Scoping with `find.descendant(of: find.byType(NavigationBar), matching: find.text(label))` would be explicit and immune to future page content that contains the label text (very likely: a Profile page will contain the word "profile", etc.). Once a page with visible text 'Home' exists, `.last` may pick the wrong one (actually page text comes before NavigationBar in the tree? Scaffold body before bottomNavigationBar → `.last` = NavigationBar label. Still fragile but currently right). SUGESTION.

**8. Missing back-behavior test**: The PR's key decision "back-from-shell doesn't return to the start screen" is asserted indirectly by `find.byType(StartPage), findsNothing` after tapping Start (app_test.dart:30-33). That actually does verify replacement since with plain push the StartPage would remain mounted in the stack and be found. OK so it IS covered. Good — no finding. Actually wait — `pumpWidget` + tap + pumpAndSetle: after pushReplacementNamed, the old route is disposed. `find.byType(StartPage)` findsNothing → verifies. Fine, covered.

- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T13:49:56Z

## PR Description

Closes #2
## What changed

Initial routing system: the app boots on a Start page that leads into a Shell page hosting the 4 main destinations — home, explore, collection, profile.

## Key decisions

- Built-in named routes (`MaterialApp.routes`, `lib/routing/app_routes.dart`) — no new dependencies for the initial system
- `StartPage` uses `pushReplacementNamed` so back-from-shell doesn't return to the start screen
- `ShellPage` switches destinations with a `NavigationBar` + `IndexedStack`, so each tab's state survives switches
- Destination order driven by the `ShellDestination` enum; pages are placeholders for future stories
- Replaced the template counter page and its smoke test with routing/shell widget tests

## How to verify

```bash
flutter test        # 10 widget tests pass
flutter analyze     # no issues
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[main] --> APP[DarkCatsFactoryApp]
  APP -->|"/"| START[StartPage]
  APP -->|"/shell"| SHELL[ShellPage]
  START -->|pushReplacementNamed /shell| SHELL
  SHELL --> NAV[NavigationBar]
  SHELL --> STACK[IndexedStack]
  STACK --> H[HomePage]
  STACK --> E[ExplorePage]
  STACK --> C[CollectionPage]
  STACK --> P[ProfilePage]
```

</details>

Now, deep-review analysis. Let me think through the findings carefully:

### Findings candidates:

**1. `_icons[destination]!` null assertions + records `.$1`/`.$2`** (shell_page.dart:55-58)
- Safe at runtime since map covers all enum values, but `!` assertions and positional record accessors `.$1`/`.$2` are unreadable and fragile if a new enum value is added without an icon entry (runtime crash at first build of that destination). Alternative: exhaustive switch expression — Dart exhaustiveness checking on enums would make adding a new destination a compile error. This is a real maintainability point. IMPORTANT or SUGESTION?
 - A `switch (destination)` expression over an enum is exhaustively checked by the compiler; a map lookup with `!` fails only at runtime. For a codebase intended to grow (4 destinations, future stories), the switch is meaningfully safer. But it's still "works as shipped" → per verdict rules: correctness/bug findings = BLOCKING only if broken behavior. This is a latent-crash risk on future extension, not current bug. I'd rate IMPORTANT (real maintainability debt).

**2. `capitalize` private extension in shell_page.dart** (line 72-74)
- Unamed `extension on String` in a page widget file. Works, but it's a general-purpose string utility living in shell_page.dart; when another file needs capitalization they'd copy it. Also unnamed private extension silently applies to all Strings in this file. Move to `lib/common/` or name it. SUGESTION.

**3. `_pages.values.toList(growable: false)`** (line 48)
- Depends on map insertion order implicitly. Since Dart maps preserve insertion order it's correct, but a `List` constant (or `IndexedStack(children: [...])` derived from an iterable of destinations) would make the "order == enum order" contract explicit. Could merge with finding 1 as one comment about enum-driven lookups. Actually I'll keep them separate but small.

Actually, let me consolidate: one inline comment on shell_page.dart build method / maps about exhaustive switch instead of map+`!`. And maybe a separate one about the extension.

**4. MaterialApp lacks `onGenerateRoute`/`onUnknownRoute`** (app.dart:23-28)
- With `routes:` map only, navigating to an undefined route (deep link typo, future code calling pushNamed('/settings')) throws in debug and shows red screen. Since this PR is "initial routing system", wiring `onGenerateRoute` centralizing route resolution (or at least `onUnknownRoute`) would be the natural foundation. SUGESTION/IMPORTANT? The PR scope is initial routing; unknown-route handling is arguably part of a routing foundation. But it's not a bug today — all navigation goes through defined constants. I'd say SUGESTION. Hmm. For an "initial routing system" PR, adding onUnknownRoute early is cheap and prevents future crashes. But severity-wise: no current breakage → SUGESTION.

**5. `initialRoute` param "used by tests"** (app.dart:9-12)
- Test-only production parameter. It's a common, pragmatic pattern; documented. SUGESTION-level at most. Actually it's fine — many projects do this; the doc comment explains it. Skip or mention as fine. I'll skip — not a finding. Hmm, alternatively could suggest `@visibleForTesting` annotation to enforce. That's a nice small suggestion: annotate with `@visibleForTesting`? No wait — it's a constructor param used by tests only, annotating the field with `@visibleForTesting` is exactly the idiomatic way to encode "used by tests". Good small SUGESTION with concrete fix.

**6. `.gitignore` adds `/input/` and `/outputs/`** — unrelated to routing (harness housekeeping). Minor scope note. Given the repo is an agent-factory repo, it's pragmatic; the PR description doesn't mention it. SUGESTION-level note (scope transparency) or skip? The guidelines say flag scope creep. It's 3 lines, harmless, and self-documented ("Agent task harness artifacts (not part of the app)"). I'd note it in general comment, not inline. Or a tiny inline suggestion. I'll include as SUGESTION inline on the .gitignore line, asking to either mention it in PR description or split. Actually per the diff checklist "Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep?" — yes flag it, but SUGESTION severity.

**7. Test britleness: `tapDestination` uses `find.text(label).last`** (shell_page_test.dart:19-22)
- `.last` relies on widget-tree order to disambiguate the NavigationBar label from page content text (pages show the same strings: 'Home', 'Explore'...). Currently at tap time the target page is offstage so `find.text` (skipOffstage:true) matches only the nav label; `.last` is unnecessary-but-defensive. Scoping with `find.descendant(of: find.byType(NavigationBar), matching: find.text(label))` would be explicit and immune to future page content that contains the label text (very likely: a Profile page will contain the word "profile", etc.). Once a page with visible text 'Home' exists, `.last` may pick the wrong one (actually page text comes before NavigationBar in the tree? Scaffold body before bottomNavigationBar → `.last` = NavigationBar label. Still fragile but currently right). SUGESTION.

**8. Missing back-behavior test**: The PR's key decision "back-from-shell doesn't return to the start screen" is asserted indirectly by `find.byType(StartPage), findsNothing` after tapping Start (app_test.dart:30-33). That actually does verify replacement since with plain push the StartPage would remain mounted in the stack and be found. OK so it IS covered. Good — no finding. Actually wait — `pumpWidget` + tap + pumpAndSetle: after pushReplacementNamed, the old route is disposed. `find.byType(StartPage)` findsNothing → verifies. Fine, covered.

**9. Deep-link initialRoute stack shape**: test pumps `DarkCatsFactoryApp(initialRoute: AppRoutes.shell)`. Flutter's default initial-routes generation for '/shell': it tries to push '/' first? Let me verify with the local SDK source to be accurate, because IF Navigator pushes '/' (StartPage) below '/shell', then a hardware back from Shell would land on Start — contradicting the PR's stated decision. This confirms the key behavior: `Navigator.defaultGenerateInitialRoutes` for `initialRoute: '/shell'`:

1. `result.add(_routeNamed('/', allowNull: true))` — pushes the **'/' route (StartPage)** first!
2. Then `result.add(_routeNamed('/shell', allowNull: true))` — pushes ShellPage on top.

So the initial stack for a `/shell` deep link is `[StartPage, ShellPage]` — **the StartPage IS underneath the ShellPage**. The PR's stated key decision — "`StartPage` uses `pushReplacementNamed` so back-from-shell doesn't return to the start screen" — holds only for the in-app navigation path (tap Start → pushReplacement → stack = [ShellPage]). But if the app is launched with `initialRoute: '/shell'` (deep link, or the test path), the stack is [StartPage('/', ), ShellPage], and system back from Shell **would** return to the Start screen.

Is this a real-world scenario? Deep links into the app (e.g., Android intent, or restoring state) with `/shell` route would show this. It's an edge case for this stage of the app (no deep-link infrastructure configured — no intent filters probably), but it IS a real inconsistency with the PR's stated decision, and it's exactly the kind of subtle routing behavior the "initial routing system" should get right or at least document.

Severity: The app currently doesn't declare deep links, and the only way to hit `/shell` as initial route is the test. So it's not a user-facing bug today. But it is a correctness trap: the stated invariant "back-from-shell doesn't return to start" is not enforced on the deep-link path. I'd rate it ⚠️ IMPORTANT with a concrete fix suggestion:

Option A: keep `routes` but note the caveat / add a test documenting the stack shape.
Option B: handle it in ShellPage with PopScope or in app with `onGenerateInitialRoutes` that returns only [shell] when initialRoute == '/shell'.

## PR Description

Closes #2
## What changed

Initial routing system: the app boots on a Start page that leads into a Shell page hosting the 4 main destinations — home, explore, collection, profile.

## Key decisions

- Built-in named routes (`MaterialApp.routes`, `lib/routing/app_routes.dart`) — no new dependencies for the initial system
- `StartPage` uses `pushReplacementNamed` so back-from-shell doesn't return to the start screen
- `ShellPage` switches destinations with a `NavigationBar` + `IndexedStack`, so each tab's state survives switches
- Destination order driven by the `ShellDestination` enum; pages are placeholders for future stories

# pr-3: gh-2 Create initial routing system

## Description

Closes #2
## What changed

Initial routing system: the app boots on a Start page that leads into a Shell page hosting the 4 main destinations — home, explore, collection, profile.

## Key decisions

- Built-in named routes (`MaterialApp.routes`, `lib/routing/app_routes.dart`) — no new dependencies for the initial system
- `StartPage` uses `pushReplacementNamed` so back-from-shell doesn't return to the start screen
- `ShellPage` switches destinations with a `NavigationBar` + `IndexedStack`, so each tab's state survives switches
- Destination order driven by the `ShellDestination` enum; pages are placeholders for future stories
- Replaced the template counter page and its smoke test with routing/shell widget tests

## How to verify

Interesting: In the diff of `lib/main.dart` removed code, I see `colorScheme: .fromSeed(seedColor: Colors.deepPurple)` and `mainAxisAlignment: .center` — this is Dart's new dot-shorthand syntax (Dart 3.10 feature). The removed code had it, so the template was created with a newer Flutter. That's fine.

Now let me look at key review points:

1. **`.gitignore` change**: adds `/input/` and `/outputs/` — agent harness artifacts. This is scope creep relative to "create initial routing system"? It's minor housekeeping, probably fine but worth noting. Actually it's reasonable to exclude these. But it's in the diff — it's arguably out of scope for a routing PR. Minor.

2. **`lib/app.dart`**:
  - `initialRoute: initialRoute` — passing nullable string. If null, MaterialApp uses default `/`. Fine.
  - `MaterialApp` without `onGenerateRoute` — unknown routes will crash in debug / show error. For a routing PR, missing `onUnknownRoute` handling. Minor/suggestion.
  - The `initialRoute` param is test-only — documented. OK.

This confirms the key behavior: `Navigator.defaultGenerateInitialRoutes` for `initialRoute: '/shell'`:

1. `result.add(_routeNamed('/', allowNull: true))` — pushes the **'/' route (StartPage)** first!
2. Then `result.add(_routeNamed('/shell', allowNull: true))` — pushes ShellPage on top.

So the initial stack for a `/shell` deep link is `[StartPage, ShellPage]` — **the StartPage IS underneath the ShellPage**. The PR's stated key decision — "`StartPage` uses `pushReplacementNamed` so back-from-shell doesn't return to the start screen" — holds only for the in-app navigation path (tap Start → pushReplacement → stack = [ShellPage]). But if the app is launched with `initialRoute: '/shell'` (deep link, or the test path), the stack is [StartPage('/', ), ShellPage], and system back from Shell **would** return to the Start screen.

Is this a real-world scenario? Deep links into the app (e.g., Android intent, or restoring state) with `/shell` route would show this. It's an edge case for this stage of the app (no deep-link infrastructure configured — no intent filters probably), but it IS a real inconsistency with the PR's stated decision, and it's exactly the kind of subtle routing behavior the "initial routing system" should get right or at least document.

Severity: The app currently doesn't declare deep links, and the only way to hit `/shell` as initial route is the test. So it's not a user-facing bug today. But it is a correctness trap: the stated invariant "back-from-shell doesn't return to start" is not enforced on the deep-link path. I'd rate it ⚠️ IMPORTANT with a concrete fix suggestion:

Option A: keep `routes` but note the caveat / add a test documenting the stack shape.
Option B: handle it in ShellPage with PopScope or in app with `onGenerateInitialRoutes` that returns only [shell] when initialRoute == '/shell'.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Map + `!` + positional record fields — not compiler-checked when a destination is added**

`shell_page.dart:32-40` stores icons in a `Map<ShellDestination, (IconData, IconData)>` and reads them with `_icons[destination]!.$1` / `!.$2` (lines 59-60). If a new `ShellDestination` value is added without a map entry, this crashes at runtime (`Null check operator used on a null value`) on the first build — nothing at compile time catches it. `.$1`/`.$2` also read as magic numbers.

An exhaustive `switch` expression over the enum turns that omission into a **compile-time error** and removes the `!`:

```dart
static (IconData, IconData> _iconsFor(ShellDestination destination) =>
    switch (destination) {
      ShellDestination.home => (Icons.home_outlined, Icons.home),
      ShellDestination.explore => (Icons.explore_outlined, Icons.explore),
      ShellDestination.collection => (
        Icons.collections_bookmark_outlined,
        Icons.collections_bookmark,
      ),
      ShellDestination.profile => (Icons.person_outline, Icons.person),
    };
```

The same applies to `_pages` (lines 25-30): its `.values` iteration order implicitly relies on map insertion order matching the enum order. A switch (or a `const` list built from a switch) makes the "order == enum order" contract explicit and exhaustively checked.

## PR Description

Closes #2
## What changed

Initial routing system: the app boots on a Start page that leads into a Shell page hosting the 4 main destinations — home, explore, collection, profile.

## Key decisions

- Built-in named routes (`MaterialApp.routes`, `lib/routing/app_routes.dart`) — no new dependencies for the initial system
- `StartPage` uses `pushReplacementNamed` so back-from-shell doesn't return to the start screen
- `ShellPage` switches destinations with a `NavigationBar` + `IndexedStack`, so each tab's state survives switches
- Destination order driven by the `ShellDestination` enum; pages are placeholders for future stories
- Replaced the template counter page and its smoke test with routing/shell widget tests

## How to verify

```bash
flutter test        # 10 widget tests pass
flutter analyze     # no issues
```

```mermaid
  SHELL --> STACK[IndexedStack]
  STACK --> H[HomePage]
  STACK --> E[ExplorePage]
  STACK --> C[CollectionPage]
  STACK --> P[ProfilePage]
```

</details>

Now let me look at key review points:

1. **`.gitignore` change**: adds `/input/` and `/outputs/` — agent harness artifacts. This is scope creep relative to "create initial routing system"? 2. **`lib/app.dart`**:
  - `initialRoute: initialRoute` — passing nullable string. If null, MaterialApp uses default `/`. Fine.
  - `MaterialApp` without `onGenerateRoute` — unknown routes will crash in debug / show error. For a routing PR, missing `onUnknownRoute` handling. Minor/suggestion.

  - Theme duplicated? The old main.dart had theme with deepPurple seed; new app.dart keeps it. Fine.

3. **`lib/main.dart`** — now just boots the app. Fine.

4. **`lib/routing/app_routes.dart`**:
  - `abstract final class AppRoutes` with static consts. Fine, modern Dart.
  - Route `start = '/'`. Note: with `MaterialApp.routes` and `initialRoute` default `'/'`, the `/` route is the start page. OK.
  - Potential issue: `onGenerateRoute` not set; deep links to unknown routes → error page. Minor.

5. **`lib/pages/shell_page.dart`**:
  - `enum ShellDestination { home, explore, collection, profile }` — public enum used to drive order.
  - `_icons` map uses records `(IconData, IconData)`.
  - `_icons[destination]!` — null assertion; safe because map covers all values. Could use `._` lookups... fine.
  - `capitalize` extension is private (unnamed extension `extension on String`). It's defined in the same file at the bottom. Private extension in a page file — could be a util. Minor.
  - `ShellDestination.values[index]` — index from NavigationBar; safe.
  - **Potential issue**: `IndexedStack` keeps all 4 pages mounted — fine for placeholders, but state claim "each tab's state survives" — yes.
  - **Deep-link/URL issue**: with named routes, `/shell` state (selected tab) isn't in the route. Not a big deal for this stage.
  - **Important correctness nuance**: `Navigator.of(context).pushReplacementNamed(AppRoutes.shell)` — then within ShellPage, back button (Android system back) exits app. Fine.
  - `_pages` is `static const Map<ShellDestination, Widget>`; `_pages.values.toList(growable: false)` — the order of Map literal values follows insertion order which matches enum order. OK.
  - The tuple `_icons[destination]!.$1` and `.$2` — using record positional fields; a bit cryptic; could be a small data class or two maps. Suggestion-level.

6. **`lib/pages/start_page.dart`**:
  - `pushReplacementNamed` — good.
  - The button label 'Start' — fine.

7. **Tests**:
  - `test/app_test.dart` — 4 tests.
  - `test/shell_page_test.dart` — 6 tests. Total 10 — matches PR description "10 widget tests".
  - `tapDestination` uses `find.text(label).last` — why `.last`? Because the label text may also appear in page content (e.g., 'Home' text in HomePage center and in NavigationBar). Actually pages show text 'Home', 'Explore', etc. So `find.text('Explore')` matches both the nav label and the page text. `.last` picks the NavigationBar one (nav bar is later in tree? Actually body is built before bottomNavigationBar in Scaffold... but with IndexedStack offstage pages also present). Hmm, `find.text('Explore')` before tapping: initially only 'Explore' nav label visible (ExplorePage offstage? No — IndexedStack mounts all children, so ExplorePage's Text('Explore') is in the tree but offstage). By default `find.text` has `skipOffstage: true`, so initially only the NavigationBar label matches. After navigating to Explore, both are visible... wait, but in tapDestination, we tap before the page is shown, so only nav label visible at tap time. `.last` is defensive. But wait — `find.text('Collection')` when tapping Collection initially: only nav label. OK.
  - In the 'shell offers the four destinations' test they use `find.descendant(of: navigationBar, matching: find.text('Home'))` — good scoping.
  - `testWidgets('home is the initial destination')` — expects ExplorePage findsNothing — works due to skipOffstage default true.
  - Tests look reasonable. One britleness: `tapDestination` with `.last` relies on widget order; fine.
  - No test for Android back from shell returning to... pushReplacement means back exits. No test needed.
  - No `flutter_test` config for fonts/assets; fine.

8. **Missing things**:
  - No `onGenerateRoute`/`onUnknownRoute`: navigating to an undefined route throws. For initial routing system, might be worth a suggestion.
  - `AppBar`? Shell has no app bar — placeholders.
  - The `capitalize` extension is `extension on String` (unnamed/private) — usable only within shell_page.dart. Fine but if needed elsewhere later, move to a shared util. Suggestion.
  - Potential a11y/semantics: NavigationBar destinations fine.
  - `Colors.deepPurple` — matches template. Fine.
  - **Tests count**: PR says 10 widget tests pass. app_test (4) + shell_page_test (6) = 10. ✓.

```dart
      ShellDestination.profile => (Icons.person_outline, Icons.person),
    };
```

The same applies to `_pages` (lines 25-30): its `.values` iteration order implicitly relies on map insertion order matching the enum order. A switch (or a `const` list built from a switch) makes the "order == enum order" contract explicit and exhaustively checked.

blocks.text:
Now I have the full diff. Let me review the changed files deeply. Let me also look at the project structure, AGENTS.md (if it exists), and the instructions.md at repo root (mentioned in guidelines).

Let me check:
1. instruction.md at repo root — project stack, conventions
2. AGENTS.md — coding styles
3. The repo structure

Interesting: In the diff of `lib/main.dart` removed code, I see `colorScheme: .fromSeed(seedColor: Colors.deepPurple)` and `mainAxisAlignment: .center` — this is Dart's new dot-shorthand syntax (Dart 3.10 feature). The removed code had it, so the template was created with a newer Flutter. That's fine.

Now let me look at key review points:

1. **`.gitignore` change**: adds `/input/` and `/outputs/` — agent harness artifacts. This is scope creep relative to "create initial routing system"? It's minor housekeeping, probably fine but worth noting. Actually it's reasonable to exclude these. But it's in the diff — it's arguably out of scope for a routing PR. Minor.

2. **`lib/app.dart`**:
  - `initialRoute: initialRoute` — passing nullable string. If null, MaterialApp uses default `/`. Fine.
  - `MaterialApp` without `onGenerateRoute` — unknown routes will crash in debug / show error. For a routing PR, missing `onUnknownRoute` handling. Minor/suggestion.
  - The `initialRoute` param is test-only — documented. OK.
  - Theme duplicated? The old main.dart had theme with deepPurple seed; new app.dart keeps it. Fine.

3. **`lib/main.dart`** — now just boots the app. Fine.

4. **`lib/routing/app_routes.dart`**:
  - `abstract final class AppRoutes` with static consts. Fine, modern Dart.
  - Route `start = '/'`. Note: with `MaterialApp.routes` and `initialRoute` default `'/'`, the `/` route is the start page. OK.
  - Potential issue: `onGenerateRoute` not set; deep links to unknown routes → error page. Minor.

5. **`lib/pages/shell_page.dart`**:
  - `enum ShellDestination { home, explore, collection, profile }` — public enum used to drive order.
  - `_icons` map uses records `(IconData, IconData)`.
  - `_icons[destination]!` — null assertion; safe because map covers all values. Could use `._` lookups... fine.
  - `capitalize` extension is private (unnamed extension `extension on String`). It's defined in the same file at the bottom. Private extension in a page file — could be a util. Minor.
  - `ShellDestination.values[index]` — index from NavigationBar; safe.
  - **Potential issue**: `IndexedStack` keeps all 4 pages mounted — fine for placeholders, but state claim "each tab's state survives" — yes.
  - **Deep-link/URL issue**: with named routes, `/shell` state (selected tab) isn't in the route. Not a big deal for this stage.
  - **Important correctness nuance**: `Navigator.of(context).pushReplacementNamed(AppRoutes.shell)` — then within ShellPage, back button (Android system back) exits app. Fine.
  - `_pages` is `static const Map<ShellDestination, Widget>`; `_pages.values.toList(growable: false)` — the order of Map literal values follows insertion order which matches enum order. OK.
  - The tuple `_icons[destination]!.$1` and `.$2` — using record positional fields; a bit cryptic; could be a small data class or two maps. Suggestion-level.

6. **`lib/pages/start_page.dart`**:
  - `pushReplacementNamed` — good.
  - The button label 'Start' — fine.

7. **Tests**:
  - `test/app_test.dart` — 4 tests.
  - `test/shell_page_test.dart` — 6 tests. Total 10 — matches PR description "10 widget tests".
  - `tapDestination` uses `find.text(label).last` — why `.last`? Because the label text may also appear in page content (e.g., 'Home' text in HomePage center and in NavigationBar). Actually pages show text 'Home', 'Explore', etc. So `find.text('Explore')` matches both the nav label and the page text. `.last` picks the NavigationBar one (nav bar is later in tree? Actually body is built before bottomNavigationBar in Scaffold... but with IndexedStack offstage pages also present). Hmm, `find.text('Explore')` before tapping: initially only 'Explore' nav label visible (ExplorePage offstage? No — IndexedStack mounts all children, so ExplorePage's Text('Explore') is in the tree but offstage). By default `find.text` has `skipOffstage: true`, so initially only the NavigationBar label matches. After navigating to Explore, both are visible... wait, but in tapDestination, we tap before the page is shown, so only nav label visible at tap time. `.last` is defensive. But wait — `find.text('Collection')` when tapping Collection initially: only nav label. OK.

This confirms the key behavior: `Navigator.defaultGenerateInitialRoutes` for `initialRoute: '/shell'`:

1. `result.add(_routeNamed('/', allowNull: true))` — pushes the **'/' route (StartPage)** first!
2. Then `result.add(_routeNamed('/shell', allowNull: true))` — pushes ShellPage on top.

So the initial stack for a `/shell` deep link is `[StartPage, ShellPage]` — **the StartPage IS underneath the ShellPage**. The PR's stated key decision — "`StartPage` uses `pushReplacementNamed` so back-from-shell doesn't return to the start screen" — holds only for the in-app navigation path (tap Start → pushReplacement → stack = [ShellPage]). But if the app is launched with `initialRoute: '/shell'` (deep link, or the test path), the stack is [StartPage('/', ), ShellPage], and system back from Shell **would** return to the Start screen.

Is this a real-world scenario? Deep links into the app (e.g., Android intent, or restoring state) with `/shell` route would show this. It's an edge case for this stage of the app (no deep-link infrastructure configured — no intent filters probably), but it IS a real inconsistency with the PR's stated decision, and it's exactly the kind of subtle routing behavior the "initial routing system" should get right or at least document.

Severity: The app currently doesn't declare deep links, and the only way to hit `/shell` as initial route is the test. So it's not a user-facing bug today. But it is a correctness trap: the stated invariant "back-from-shell doesn't return to start" is not enforced on the deep-link path. I'd rate it ⚠️ IMPORTANT with a concrete fix suggestion:

Option A: keep `routes` but note the caveat / add a test documenting the stack shape.
Option B: handle it in ShellPage with PopScope or in app with `onGenerateInitialRoutes` that returns only [shell] when initialRoute == '/shell'.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Map + `!` + positional record fields — not compiler-checked when a destination is added**

`shell_page.dart:32-40` stores icons in a `Map<ShellDestination, (IconData, IconData)>` and reads them with `_icons[destination]!.$1` / `!.$2` (lines 59-60). If a new `ShellDestination` value is added without a map entry, this crashes at runtime (`Null check operator used on a null value`) on the first build — nothing at compile time catches it. `.$1`/`.$2` also read as magic numbers.

An exhaustive `switch` expression over the enum turns that omission into a **compile-time error** and removes the `!`:

```dart
static (IconData, IconData> _iconsFor(ShellDestination destination) =>
    switch (destination) {
      ShellDestination.home => (Icons.home_outlined, Icons.home),
      ShellDestination.explore => (Icons.explore_outlined, Icons.explore),
      ShellDestination.collection => (
        Icons.collections_bookmark_outlined,
        Icons.collections_bookmark,
      ),
      ShellDestination.profile => (Icons.person_outline, Icons.person),
    };
```

The same applies to `_pages` (lines 25-30): its `.values` iteration order implicitly relies on map insertion order matching the enum order. A switch (or a `const` list built from a switch) makes the "order == enum order" contract explicit and exhaustively checked.

💡 **SUGGESTION: Add an unknown-route fallback as part of the routing foundation**

The app routes only through the `routes` map — there is no `onGenerateRoute`/`onUnknownRoute`. Any navigation to an undefined name (a `pushNamed('/setings')` typo, a future deep link, or a platform intent) throws `onGenerateRoute returned null` and shows the grey/red error screen instead of a graceful fallback.

Since this PR establishes the initial routing system, wiring a fallback now is cheap and self-documenting:

```dart
MaterialApp(
  routes: {
    AppRoutes.start: (context) => const StartPage(),
    AppRoutes.shell: (context) => const ShellPage(),
  },
  onUnknownRoute: (settings) => MaterialPageRoute<dynamic>(
    builder: (context) => const StartPage(), // or a dedicated NotFoundPage
  ),
)
```

Optional at this stage — all current navigation goes through `AppRoutes` constants.

💡 **SUGGESTION: `.gitignore` change is outside the routing scope**

The only change to `.gitignore` adds harness artifact paths (`/input/`, `/outputs/`) — unrelated to the routing system gh-2 describes, and not mentioned in the PR description's "What changed" list.

The change itself is sensible housekeeping for this factory-managed repo (it also fixes the missing trailing newline), so keeping it is fine — just add one line to the PR description (e.g. "Also ignores local agent harness artifacts") or split it into a separate `chore:` commit so the history stays greppable. (As a bonus, it incidentally fixes the file's missing trailing newline.)

Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 3
- **URL**: https://github.com/Vovanella95/dark_cats_factory/pull/3
- **Title**: gh-2 Create initial routing system
- **Author**: Vovanella95
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-2` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 13
- **Additions**: +331
- **Deletions**: -149
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T13:49:29Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T13:49:56Z

## PR Description

Closes #2
## What changed

Initial routing system: the app boots on a Start page that leads into a Shell page hosting the 4 main destinations — home, explore, collection, profile.

## Key decisions

- Built-in named routes (`MaterialApp.routes`, `lib/routing/app_routes.dart`) — no new dependencies for the initial system
- `StartPage` uses `pushReplacementNamed` so back-from-shell doesn't return to the start screen
- `ShellPage` switches destinations with a `NavigationBar` + `IndexedStack`, so each tab's state survives switches
- Destination order driven by the `ShellDestination` enum; pages are placeholders for future stories
- Replaced the template counter page and its smoke test with routing/shell widget tests

## How to verify

```bash
flutter test        # 10 widget tests pass
flutter analyze     # no issues
```

<details>
<summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  M[main] --> APP[DarkCatsFactoryApp]
  APP -->|"/"| START[StartPage]
  APP -->|"/shell"| SHELL[ShellPage]
  START -->|pushReplacementNamed /shell| SHELL
  SHELL --> NAV[NavigationBar]
  SHELL --> STACK[IndexedStack]
  STACK --> H[HomePage]
  STACK --> E[ExplorePage]
  STACK --> C[CollectionPage]
  STACK --> P[ProfilePage]
```

</details>

**1. `_icons[destination]!` null assertions + records `.$1`/`.$2`** (shell_page.dart:55-58)

Alternative: exhaustive switch expression — Dart exhaustiveness checking on enums would make adding a new destination a compile error. This is a real maintainability point. IMPORTANT or SUGESTION?
 - A `switch (destination)` expression over an enum is exhaustively checked by the compiler; a map lookup with `!` fails only at runtime. For a codebase intended to grow (4 destinations, future stories), the switch is meaningfully safer. But it's still "works as shipped" → per verdict rules: correctness/bug findings = BLOCKING only if broken behavior. This is a latent-crash risk on future extension, not current bug. I'd rate IMPORTANT (real maintainability debt).

**2. `capitalize` private extension in shell_page.dart** (line 72-74)
- Unamed `extension on String` in a page widget file. Works, but it's a general-purpose string utility living in shell_page.dart; when another file needs capitalization they'd copy it. Also unnamed private extension silently applies to all Strings in this file. Move to `lib/common/` or name it. SUGESTION.

## PR Description

Closes #2
## What changed

Initial routing system: the app boots on a Start page that leads into a Shell page hosting the 4 main destinations — home, explore, collection, profile.

## Key decisions

- Built-in named routes (`MaterialApp.routes`, `lib/routing/app_routes.dart`) — no new dependencies for the initial system
- `StartPage` uses `pushReplacementNamed` so back-from-shell doesn't return to the start screen
- `ShellPage` switches destinations with a `NavigationBar` + `IndexedStack`, so each tab's state survives switches
- Destination order driven by the `ShellDestination` enum; pages are placeholders for future stories
- Replaced the template counter page and its smoke test with routing/shell widget tests

```bash
flutter test        # 10 widget tests pass
flutter analyze     # no issues
```

blocks.text:
Now I have the full diff. Let me review the changed files deeply. Let me also look at the project structure, AGENTS.md (if it exists), and the instructions.md at repo root (mentioned in guidelines).

Let me check:
1. instruction.md at repo root — project stack, conventions
2. AGENTS.md — coding styles
3. The repo structure

Interesting: In the diff of `lib/main.dart` removed code, I see `colorScheme: .fromSeed(seedColor: Colors.deepPurple)` and `mainAxisAlignment: .center` — this is Dart's new dot-shorthand syntax (Dart 3.10 feature). The removed code had it, so the template was created with a newer Flutter. That's fine.

Now let me look at key review points:

1. **`.gitignore` change**: adds `/input/` and `/outputs/` — agent harness artifacts. This is scope creep relative to "create initial routing system"? It's minor housekeeping, probably fine but worth noting. Actually it's reasonable to exclude these. But it's in the diff — it's arguably out of scope for a routing PR. Minor.

2. **`lib/app.dart`**:
  - `initialRoute: initialRoute` — passing nullable string. If null, MaterialApp uses default `/`. Fine.
  - `MaterialApp` without `onGenerateRoute` — unknown routes will crash in debug / show error. For a routing PR, missing `onUnknownRoute` handling. Minor/suggestion.
  - The `initialRoute` param is test-only — documented. OK.
  - Theme duplicated? The old main.dart had theme with deepPurple seed; new app.dart keeps it. Fine.

3. **`lib/main.dart`** — now just boots the app. Fine.

4. **`lib/routing/app_routes.dart`**:
  - `abstract final class AppRoutes` with static consts. Fine, modern Dart.
  - Route `start = '/'`. Note: with `MaterialApp.routes` and `initialRoute` default `'/'`, the `/` route is the start page. OK.
  - Potential issue: `onGenerateRoute` not set; deep links to unknown routes → error page. Minor.

5. **`lib/pages/shell_page.dart`**:
  - `enum ShellDestination { home, explore, collection, profile }` — public enum used to drive order.
  - `_icons` map uses records `(IconData, IconData)`.
  - `_icons[destination]!` — null assertion; safe because map covers all values. Could use `._` lookups... fine.
  - `capitalize` extension is private (unnamed extension `extension on String`). It's defined in the same file at the bottom. Private extension in a page file — could be a util. Minor.
  - `ShellDestination.values[index]` — index from NavigationBar; safe.
  - **Potential issue**: `IndexedStack` keeps all 4 pages mounted — fine for placeholders, but state claim "each tab's state survives" — yes.
  - **Deep-link/URL issue**: with named routes, `/shell` state (selected tab) isn't in the route. Not a big deal for this stage.
  - **Important correctness nuance**: `Navigator.of(context).pushReplacementNamed(AppRoutes.shell)` — then within ShellPage, back button (Android system back) exits app. Fine.
  - `_pages` is `static const Map<ShellDestination, Widget>`; `_pages.values.toList(growable: false)` — the order of Map literal values follows insertion order which matches enum order. OK.
  - The tuple `_icons[destination]!.$1` and `.$2` — using record positional fields; a bit cryptic; could be a small data class or two maps. Suggestion-level.

6. **`lib/pages/start_page.dart`**:
  - `pushReplacementNamed` — good.
  - The button label 'Start' — fine.

7. **Tests**:
  - `test/app_test.dart` — 4 tests.
  - `test/shell_page_test.dart` — 6 tests. Total 10 — matches PR description "10 widget tests".
  - `tapDestination` uses `find.text(label).last` — why `.last`? Because the label text may also appear in page content (e.g., 'Home' text in HomePage center and in NavigationBar). Actually pages show text 'Home', 'Explore', etc. So `find.text('Explore')` matches both the nav label and the page text. `.last` picks the NavigationBar one (nav bar is later in tree? Actually body is built before bottomNavigationBar in Scaffold... but with IndexedStack offstage pages also present). Hmm, `find.text('Explore')` before tapping: initially only 'Explore' nav label visible (ExplorePage offstage? No — IndexedStack mounts all children, so ExplorePage's Text('Explore') is in the tree but offstage). By default `find.text` has `skipOffstage: true`, so initially only the NavigationBar label matches. After navigating to Explore, both are visible... wait, but in tapDestination, we tap before the page is shown, so only nav label visible at tap time. `.last` is defensive. But wait — `find.text('Collection')` when tapping Collection initially: only nav label. OK.

This confirms the key behavior: `Navigator.defaultGenerateInitialRoutes` for `initialRoute: '/shell'`:

1. `result.add(_routeNamed('/', allowNull: true))` — pushes the **'/' route (StartPage)** first!
2. Then `result.add(_routeNamed('/shell', allowNull: true))` — pushes ShellPage on top.

So the initial stack for a `/shell` deep link is `[StartPage, ShellPage]` — **the StartPage IS underneath the ShellPage**. The PR's stated key decision — "`StartPage` uses `pushReplacementNamed` so back-from-shell doesn't return to the start screen" — holds only for the in-app navigation path (tap Start → pushReplacement → stack = [ShellPage]). But if the app is launched with `initialRoute: '/shell'` (deep link, or the test path), the stack is [StartPage('/', ), ShellPage], and system back from Shell **would** return to the Start screen.

Is this a real-world scenario? Deep links into the app (e.g., Android intent, or restoring state) with `/shell` route would show this. It's an edge case for this stage of the app (no deep-link infrastructure configured — no intent filters probably), but it IS a real inconsistency with the PR's stated decision, and it's exactly the kind of subtle routing behavior the "initial routing system" should get right or at least document.

Severity: The app currently doesn't declare deep links, and the only way to hit `/shell` as initial route is the test. So it's not a user-facing bug today. But it is a correctness trap: the stated invariant "back-from-shell doesn't return to start" is not enforced on the deep-link path. I'd rate it ⚠️ IMPORTANT with a concrete fix suggestion:

Option A: keep `routes` but note the caveat / add a test documenting the stack shape.
Option B: handle it in ShellPage with PopScope or in app with `onGenerateInitialRoutes` that returns only [shell] when initialRoute == '/shell'.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Map + `!` + positional record fields — not compiler-checked when a destination is added**

`shell_page.dart:32-40` stores icons in a `Map<ShellDestination, (IconData, IconData)>` and reads them with `_icons[destination]!.$1` / `!.$2` (lines 59-60). If a new `ShellDestination` value is added without a map entry, this crashes at runtime (`Null check operator used on a null value`) on the first build — nothing at compile time catches it. `.$1`/`.$2` also read as magic numbers.

An exhaustive `switch` expression over the enum turns that omission into a **compile-time error** and removes the `!`:

```dart
static (IconData, IconData> _iconsFor(ShellDestination destination) =>
    switch (destination) {
      ShellDestination.home => (Icons.home_outlined, Icons.home),
      ShellDestination.explore => (Icons.explore_outlined, Icons.explore),
      ShellDestination.collection => (
        Icons.collections_bookmark_outlined,
        Icons.collections_bookmark,
      ),
      ShellDestination.profile => (Icons.person_outline, Icons.person),
    };
```

The same applies to `_pages` (lines 25-30): its `.values` iteration order implicitly relies on map insertion order matching the enum order. A switch (or a `const` list built from a switch) makes the "order == enum order" contract explicit and exhaustively checked.
